title: the DSG defensive point values and the hypothermia optional rule

banner.title: The DSG DPV AND HYPOTHERMIA, R513: the printed pp. 40-42 (pdf 41-43) - the defensive point values section (the DMG page-110 fortification seam, the natural and constructed formations assigned DPVs, the destroy-on-attack-or-spell use, the cubic-open-space reading where the value is the damage needed to collapse the ceiling, the chain-reaction follow-up check after a collapse, and the Table 19 thirteen-formation grid - room 10-ft tube 50, room 20-ft cube 90, column 3-ft 10, column 10-ft 100, wall 10-ft square 20, bridge small wooden 12, bridge small stone 40, bridge large stone 80, rock ledge per 1-ft 10, ceiling small cavern 100, ceiling large cavern 250, stalactite small 8, stalactite large 20) and the hypothermia optional rule (the damp-chill preamble, the one-turn swimming onset with the no-heat-source assumption, the shallow-water risk reduction - knee-to-waist deep one hour, shallower than knee no threat - the Constitution Check after onset with 1d6 lost on a failure repeated every turn, the losses accumulating until an external heat source and even after leaving the water, the 1d6-per-turn recovery by a fire or warm-blooded creatures until fully recovered, the cold-adapted and ring-of-warmth immunity, and the grease or oil coating doubling both the time before the first check and the interval between checks)
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (idx 54 = printed p. 41, idx 55-57 = printed p. 42) - the Table 19 grid confirmed THREE WAYS: the chapter djvu read and the compiled-tables appendix reprint (djvu.txt line 15570ff) agree on all thirteen rows, with the Capture layer partially corroborating (Room 10- 50, Column 3 10, Column 10^4 diameter 100, Wall 10-fl square 20, Bridge small wooden 12, Ceiling large cavern 250; the Capture garble 104 = 10-ft and the appendix drop of the word Stalactite on the small 8 row are both settled by the chapter read). The hypothermia numbers dual-confirmed by Capture idx 56-57: the Constitution Check, the 1d6 loss per failed check, the per-turn repetition, the 1d6-per-turn recovery, the fire/warm-blooded-creature source, the ring-of-warmth immunity and the grease doubling. The Magnetic Effects of Lodestone section starts the NEXT round per the content-density rule.
banner.sentinel: Table 19 pins as a 13x2 grid: the row key and the Defensive Point Value, each the damage needed to destroy the formation (or, for a cubic open space, to collapse its ceiling). The hypothermia dice pin as dice + sides consts (loss 1d6, recovery 1d6) per the R508 convention. The DMG page-110 seam and the wsgheat.h cross-book seam are noted but nothing auto-credits; the R512 chain reaction procedure is the collapse follow-up.

consts.name: dnyT19RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 19 carries thirteen formations: two rooms, two columns, a wall, three bridges, a rock ledge, two cavern ceilings and two stalactites.

consts.name: dnySwimTurnsToOnset
consts.comment: a character becomes subject to hypothermia - a disastrous lowering of body temperature - after one turn of swimming in a typical underground body of water.

consts.name: dnyWadingOnsetHours
consts.comment: the knee-to-waist-deep wading onset delay: one hour.

consts.name: dnyLossPerFailDice
consts.comment: if the Constitution Check fails, the character loses hit points on 1d6 - the dice count.

consts.name: dnyCheckEveryTurns
consts.comment: the Constitution Check must be repeated every turn, with all hit point losses accumulating.

consts.name: dnyRecoveryPerTurnDice
consts.comment: near a heat source the character regains hit points at 1d6 per turn - the dice count.

consts.name: dnyGreaseTimeMult
consts.comment: the grease or oil coating multiplier on the time before the first Constitution Check and on the interval between checks.

bools.name: dnyFortificationsHaveDpv
bools.comment: constructed fortifications have Defensive Point Values, as explained in the DMG (page 110), and many natural and constructed underground formations are assigned DPVs too - the cross-book seam.

bools.name: dnyDpvDestroysOnAttackOrSpell
bools.comment: use these Defensive Point Values to determine if an area is destroyed by the effects of an attack or spell.

bools.name: dnyCubicOpenSpaceCeiling
bools.comment: when a Defensive Point Value is provided for a cubic open space, the value equals the amount of damage needed to cause the area's ceiling to collapse.

bools.name: dnyCollapseChecksChainReaction
bools.comment: after a DPV collapse, check for additional ceiling or wall collapses with the normal chain reaction procedure - the R512 rules/dsgcavein2.h seam.

bools.name: dnyDampChillUnhealthy
bools.comment: the damp chill of the underworld air is decidedly unhealthy for most creatures; the streams, rivers and lakes of the Underdark can numb a character who suffers prolonged exposure to their bone-chilling cold waters.

bools.name: dnyNoHeatSourceAssumed
bools.comment: the one-turn swimming onset assumes no subterranean heat source is warming the water.

bools.name: dnyShallowWaterReducesRisk
bools.comment: the risks of hypothermia are reduced in shallow water.

bools.name: dnyKneeToWaistOneHour
bools.comment: if a character is moving through water between knee and waist deep, hypothermia effects do not begin for one hour.

bools.name: dnyShallowerThanKneeNoThreat
bools.comment: if the water is shallower than knee deep, hypothermia is not a threat.

bools.name: dnyConCheckOnOnset
bools.comment: after hypothermia sets in, the player must make a Constitution Check.

bools.name: dnyLossesAccumulateUntilHeat
bools.comment: all hit point losses accumulate until the character reaches some external heat source that can warm his chilled body.

bools.name: dnyLossContinuesOutOfWater
bools.comment: hit point loss continues even after the character has gotten out of the water, if no heat source is found.

bools.name: dnyFireOrWarmCreaturesRecover
bools.comment: if a means of warming up - such as a fire or the close presence of other warm-blooded creatures - is located, the character recovers.

bools.name: dnyRecoveryUntilFullyRecovered
bools.comment: the 1d6-per-turn recovery continues until the hypothermia losses have been fully recovered.

bools.name: dnyColdAdaptedOrRingImmune
bools.comment: creatures especially adapted for cold environments, or carrying magical protections such as a ring of warmth, are not susceptible to the effects of this rule.

bools.name: dnyGreaseDoublesInterval
bools.comment: a character who thoroughly coats himself with a layer of grease or oil before entering the water can double the amount of time before making a Constitution Check, and double the interval between checks as well.
